titre: GTA 6's Long Development Cycle Even Made Rockstar Question If It Would Ever Launch
chapo: Rockstar's Rob Nelson admitted that some within studio felt like GTA 6's launch day would never come
extrait: Rockstar's Rob Nelson admitted that some within studio felt like GTA 6's launch day would never come While Grand Theft Auto 6 is real, out now, and breaking all sorts of records with how well it's selling, it felt like the game might never be released at some points during its lengthy 13-year development. In a recent interview, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that even those within Rockstar sometimes felt that way about GTA 6. Nelson, who was one of the lead developers on GTA 6, shared this sentiment in an interview with GamesRadar ahead of the game's release, saying that "it feels surreal" for the highly anticipated game to finally be out. He was also blunt that some people at Rockstar weren't sure the Nov. 19 launch of GTA 6 would ever happen because of how long it took to develop. "I think a lot of us felt like the day would never come," he explained. "A lot of us, certainly on the senior team, have shipped a fair few games. But it's been a while since we've done one of these and this one took a good chunk of time to sort of figure it out.I think it's surreal, it's a relief – we're very nervous, when you get really close to something maybe your perspective is a little bit compromised. But yeah, we're in a little bit of disbelief and we probably will be until release, and then hopefully it'll become real once people are talking about it and playing it." A 13-year development cycle is certainly unusual in the video game industry, but GTA 6 was anything but your usual AAA game. It was a sequel to one of the best-selling games of all time and had a scope far greater than most open-world games. The game's development was also elongated, as Rockstar had to focus on finishing Red Dead Redemption 2 before 2018 and then made the tough decision to delay GTA 6 a couple of times after it was officially revealed in 2022. The wait and long development cycle seem worth it in the end, as GTA 6 has been a massive success. Still, Nelson's comments show that even those at Rockstar felt the pressure and stress that comes with working on such a highly anticipated game for so long.

Even a fair few Rockstar Games workers felt like GTA 6's launch day "would never come," according to co-studio head and lead developer Rob Nelson. The wait for GTA 6 was agonizingly long for some corners of the video game world - it's been 13 years since GTA 5, eight years since Red Dead Redemption 2, and four years since we glimpsed the first set of leaks. The protracted development even led to at least one incredibly popular meme: 'We got X before GTA 6.' But GTA 6 hopefuls weren't alone in the feeling - many employees at Rockstar Games felt the same way, apparently. In an interview with GamesRadar+ ahead of launch, Nelson said "it feels surreal" to see the game finally rolling out across the world. "I think a lot of us felt like the day would never come. A lot of us, certainly on the senior team, have shipped a fair few games. But it's been a while since we've done one of these and this one took a good chunk of time to sort of figure it out. "I think it's surreal, it's a relief – we're very nervous, when you get really close to something maybe your perspective is a little bit compromised [laughter]. But yeah, we're in a little bit of disbelief and we probably will be until release, and then hopefully it'll become real once people are talking about it and playing it," he continued. And, boy, are there a lot of people playing this thing. Parent company Take-Two announced that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies before it even launched and made almost $4 billion by the end of its first day of release. The publisher has yet to reveal updated figures, but this is easily the biggest entertainment launch in history.
